papers.title: Coupled Effects of Wall Vibration and Surface Wettability on Nanoscale Liquid Film Boiling: A Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: Nanoscale liquid film boiling is a key heat transfer mechanism in high-heat-flux thermal management, but the coupled effects of wall vibration and surface wettability remain unclear. In this study, molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate water film boiling on platinum surfaces under different wettability conditions, vibration amplitudes, and vibration frequencies. The results show that surface wettability strongly regulates the balance between early nucleation and later heat transfer deterioration. Under wall vibration, the neutral-wettability case (β = 0.02) shows the mos
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how wall vibration and surface wettability jointly affect nanoscale liquid film boiling on platinum surfaces. The results show that surface wettability regulates the balance between early nucleation and later heat transfer deterioration, and under wall vibration, the neutral-wettability case exhibits the most significant enhancement in boiling heat transfer.

papers.title: Exposure-informed lung transcriptomic analysis links predicted NNK targets to cell type-specific remodeling programs in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is associated with cigarette smoking, yet the relationship between the tobacco-specific nitrosamine nicotine-derived nitrosamine ketone (NNK) and IPF-associated lung transcriptional remodeling remains incompletely understood. Here, we developed an exposure-informed computational framework integrating multi-database target prediction, lung single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic analysis, co-expression network analysis, bulk lung cohort projection, and exploratory structure-based modeling. Putative human protein targets of NNK were predicted from ChEMBL
papers.summary: This study presents a computational framework that integrates target prediction, single-cell transcriptomics, and network analysis to link the tobacco-specific carcinogen NNK to cell type-specific transcriptional remodeling in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). The findings suggest potential NNK targets that may drive disease-associated gene programs, offering a new exposure-informed perspective on IPF pathogenesis.

papers.title: Probing pyrazolo-pyrimidines as SIRT2 inhibitors via molecular modelling and biological assays.
papers.abstract: Sirtuins (SIRTs) involvement in different biological pathways opens a promising scenario for the development of related ligands to be evaluated as therapeutic agents in different diseases, such as cancer, neurodegenerative disorders, diabetes, cardiovascular and autoimmune diseases. The continuous elucidation of several SIRT2-ligand complexes fostered the discovery of novel and more selective SIRT2 inhibitors (SIRT2Is). Among them, SIRT2 in the presence of SirReal2 analogues was the most investigated. We recently reported pyrazolo-pyrimidine compounds (1-5) as SIRT2Is (1, SIRT2 % inhibition =
papers.summary: This study evaluates pyrazolo-pyrimidine compounds as selective SIRT2 inhibitors using molecular modeling and biological assays, identifying promising candidates for therapeutic applications in diseases like cancer and neurodegeneration. The work extends known SirReal2-based inhibitor design by exploring a new scaffold with improved selectivity.

papers.title: Behind substrate specificity switch in lactate dehydrogenase: Active-site loop dynamics and epistatic enhancement.
papers.abstract: Substrate specificity in lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) controls metabolic flux and remains a central challenge in enzyme engineering, particularly when closely related substrates differ by only a single carboxylate group. Although Q102 (equivalent to Gln86 in Geobacillus stearothermophilus L-LDH) is recognized as a canonical substrate-specificity determinant, how this electrostatic switch cooperates with steric effects, conformational dynamics, and scaffold context to govern substrate recognition remains unclear. Here, we combined steady-state kinetics with molecular dynamics simulations to ex
papers.summary: This study investigates how substrate specificity in lactate dehydrogenases is controlled by active-site loop dynamics and epistatic interactions, going beyond the known Q102 electrostatic switch. By combining steady-state kinetics with molecular dynamics simulations, the authors reveal that steric effects, conformational dynamics, and scaffold context cooperate to govern substrate recognition. The findings provide a more nuanced understanding of enzyme specificity that could inform engineering efforts.

papers.title: Quantifying protein unfolding kinetics with a high-throughput microfluidic platform.
papers.abstract: Even after folding, proteins sample unfolded intermediates at risk of irreversible alteration (e.g., via proteolysis, aggregation, or posttranslational modification). Thus, kinetic stability impacts protein lifetime and abundance. However, we have very few measurements of unfolding rates, largely due to technical challenges. To address this, we developed SPARKfold (simultaneous proteolysis assay revealing kinetics of folding), a microfluidic platform to express, purify, and measure unfolding rate constants at high throughput via native proteolysis. We applied SPARKfold to determine unfolding r
papers.summary: The authors developed SPARKfold, a high-throughput microfluidic platform that expresses, purifies, and measures protein unfolding rate constants via native proteolysis. This addresses the technical gap in measuring kinetic stability, which is important for understanding protein lifetime and abundance. The platform enables large-scale quantification of unfolding kinetics, providing a new tool for studying protein stability.

papers.title: Three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction by atomic force microscopy imaging and template matching allows rapid structural-based validation of recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein from a single topology image.
papers.abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) is a versatile multi-modal imaging method frequently used for structural characterisation of biological surfaces at the nanoscale. However, AFM-based three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction has hitherto not been possible due to the tip-sample convolution artifact that distorts AFM images of individual molecules, and the disconnect between two-dimensional AFM images of surface deposited molecules and their three-dimensional structures. Here, three-dimensional single-particle analysis was developed for rapid structure-based validation of protein structures
papers.summary: This paper presents a new method for three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction using atomic force microscopy (AFM) combined with template matching, overcoming the tip-sample convolution artifact that previously limited AFM structural analysis. The approach enables rapid structure-based validation of recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein from a single topology image, providing a fast and accessible alternative for protein structural verification.

papers.title: Multivalent ion binding site identification with structure-based deep learning.
papers.abstract: Protein-ion interactions are essential for many cellular processes, including enzymatic catalysis, signaling, and allosteric regulation. However, mapping ion-binding sites experimentally remains labor-intensive and expensive. Here, we present BiteNetI, a structure-based deep learning model that uses 3D convolutional neural networks to simultaneously localize ion-binding centers and predict binding residues for 14 biologically relevant ions. Trained on a carefully curated dataset of over 10,000 high-resolution protein-ion complexes, in which near-identical binding sites are consistently annotat
papers.summary: BiteNetI is a new deep learning tool that predicts where 14 different biologically relevant ions bind to proteins, identifying both the binding center and the residues involved. It was trained on a large, carefully curated dataset of over 10,000 protein-ion complexes, offering a fast and cost-effective alternative to experimental mapping of ion-binding sites.

papers.title: Development of the First YTHDC1 Degrader with Improved Antileukemia Activity.
papers.abstract: N6-Methyladenosine (m6A) represents the most prevalent internal RNA modification in eukaryotic mRNA, with YTHDC1 serving as a critical nuclear reader protein implicated in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Although selective inhibitors of YTHDC1 have been reported, whether targeted degradation of YTHDC1 could achieve enhanced therapeutic efficacy remains unexplored. Here, we report the rational design and synthesis of the first PROTAC molecule targeting YTHDC1, termed XY-2, which was developed based on the cocrystal structure of YTHDC1 bound to its known inhibitor. XY-2 efficiently induced proteas
papers.summary: This paper reports the first PROTAC degrader (XY-2) targeting the m6A reader protein YTHDC1, designed from a cocrystal structure with a known inhibitor. XY-2 induces proteasomal degradation of YTHDC1 and shows improved antileukemia activity compared to existing inhibitors, suggesting targeted degradation as a promising therapeutic strategy for AML.

papers.title: A Ligand-Triggered Receptor Conformation Enables the Design of Selective Agonists for the Dopamine 3 Receptor (D3R) Using a Bitopic Strategy.
papers.abstract: While G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) represent the largest drug target family, designing subtype-selective molecules is still a challenge, especially to distinguish among closely related subtypes. One of the most challenging cases is the distinction between dopamine D2R and D3R, pivotal receptors in motor functions and cognition, and targets of Parkinson's disease treatments, schizophrenia, or substance use disorders. Attempts to design D3R-selective molecules with ligands binding toward the first transmembrane helix (the most sequence-diverse and conformationally flexible segment in GPCR
papers.summary: This study reveals a ligand-triggered conformational change in the dopamine 3 receptor (D3R) that enables the design of subtype-selective agonists using a bitopic strategy, addressing the challenge of distinguishing D3R from the closely related D2R. The findings provide a new structural basis for developing selective drugs targeting D3R, which is relevant for treating Parkinson's disease, schizophrenia, and substance use disorders.

papers.title: Localized Rigidification and Allosteric Modulation Mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 Spike Neutralization by Class 3 and Class 4 Antibodies at Atomic Resolution: An Integrated Computational Study of Binding, Dynamics, and Allostery.
papers.abstract: The relentless evolution of SARS-CoV-2 and the emergence of highly antibody-evasive variants underscore the need to decipher the molecular principles that govern antibody neutralization breadth and resilience. In this study, we employ an integrated computational framework combining structural analysis, conformational dynamics, mutational scanning, binding energetics, and allosteric network modeling to dissect the mechanistic signatures of class 3 and class 4 antibodies targeting the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Through comprehensive analysis of antibody-RBD co
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint uses an integrated computational approach to reveal how class 3 and class 4 antibodies neutralize the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein by locally rigidifying the receptor-binding domain and modulating allosteric networks, providing atomic-level insights into binding, dynamics, and allostery that may inform broadly resilient antibody design.

papers.title: RNA G-quadruplex structure recognition by chimeric peptides.
papers.abstract: G-quadruplexes (G4s) are non-canonical nucleic acids involved in gene regulation and have attracted interest as potential therapeutic targets. However, developing ligands that selectively recognize specific G4 structures remains challenging. Here, we report the rational design of chimeric peptides that combine a de novo selected peptide (Pep11) with a native peptide (Rhau18) derived from the endogenous DHX36 protein. The chimeric peptides bound RNA G4s (rG4s) with nanomolar affinity, representing a 10-fold enhancement over the individual modules, while retaining selectivity for rG4s over DNA G
papers.summary: The authors designed chimeric peptides combining a de novo selected peptide with a native DHX36-derived peptide, achieving nanomolar-affinity binding to RNA G-quadruplexes with 10-fold improved potency over individual modules while maintaining selectivity for RNA over DNA G4s. This rational design strategy offers a new approach for developing selective RNA G4-targeting ligands.

papers.title: Structure-based screening and identification of a novel Aurora-A-targeting peptide with antiproliferative activity against prostate cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Aurora-A is a potential therapeutic target in prostate cancer. In this study, virtual screening identified four Aurora-A-targeting peptides, among which Peptide-1 showed the most favourable profile. Molecular docking and MST assays demonstrated that Peptide-1 had the lowest predicted binding free energy and the strongest binding affinity towards Aurora-A (Kd = 0.72 ± 0.04 μM). MD simulation, MM/PBSA, and free-energy landscape analyses indicated that the Aurora-A-Peptide-1 complex was conformationally stable and mainly driven by electrostatic interactions. MTT assays showed that Peptide-1 inhib
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening to identify a novel peptide (Peptide-1) that binds Aurora-A with high affinity and inhibits prostate cancer cell proliferation. The peptide forms a stable complex with Aurora-A driven by electrostatic interactions, suggesting it could be a promising lead for targeted cancer therapy.

papers.title: Potential targets and molecular mechanisms of D-pinitol against acute kidney injury based on network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a severe clinical syndrome, with ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) being one of its most common causes. Although D‑pinitol (DP), an inositol‑like bioactive molecule, is known to confer renal protection, its efficacy against I/R‑induced AKI remains unknown. A mouse kidney I/R model was employed to evaluate the renoprotective effect of DP. Relevant targets associated with DP and AKI were retrieved from publicly available databases. Subsequently, network pharmacology analysis was conducted to identify the potential targets and signaling pathways. Molecular docking was then p
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and experimental validation in a mouse kidney ischemia/reperfusion model to identify potential targets and molecular mechanisms by which D-pinitol protects against acute kidney injury. The findings suggest that D-pinitol exerts renoprotective effects through specific signaling pathways, providing a basis for its therapeutic use in AKI.

papers.title: A systematic evaluation framework for universal antibody-antigen binding affinity prediction and candidate recommendation.
papers.abstract: Predicting antigen-antibody binding is essential to drug discovery and protein engineering. For de novo antibody design, generalizable binding prediction models are crucial for efficient in silico screening. However, existing affinity predictors lack generalization, with performance deteriorating for antibodies targeting antigens absent from training data or datasets lacking non-binders. To address this, we establish a benchmarking framework for evaluating universal antibody-antigen binding affinity prediction. Our framework compares sequence- and structure-based methods across diverse antigen
papers.summary: This paper introduces a benchmarking framework to evaluate universal antibody-antigen binding affinity prediction, addressing the lack of generalization in existing models when tested on unseen antigens or datasets without non-binders. The framework compares sequence- and structure-based methods across diverse antigens, providing a systematic approach for assessing and recommending predictive models for drug discovery and protein engineering.

papers.title: Microbial levan potentiates hepatic retention and antitumor activity of a PEGylated benzimidazole-curcumin nanocomplex through TLR2-FXR/FGF15-associated immunometabolic remodeling in experimental liver cancer.
papers.abstract: Despite major advances in nanomedicine, therapeutic efficacy remains constrained by unfavorable host responses that influence nanotherapeutic retention, biodistribution, and activity. Biological strategies capable of enhancing nanomedicine performance through modulation of host-response pathways, rather than additional nanoparticle engineering, remain largely unexplored. Herein, we investigated whether a microbial levan produced by Weissella paramesenteroides could potentiate the therapeutic activity of a PEGylated β-cyclodextrin-capped benzimidazole-curcumin nanocomplex (BMPE-Cur) in an Ehrli
papers.summary: This study shows that a microbial levan from Weissella paramesenteroides enhances the liver retention and antitumor efficacy of a PEGylated curcumin nanocomplex in a mouse model of liver cancer. The effect is mediated through TLR2 and FXR/FGF15 signaling, which remodel the hepatic immune-metabolic environment to favor nanomedicine activity. This work highlights a biological strategy—using a prebiotic polymer—to boost nanotherapy performance without additional nanoparticle engineering.

papers.title: Identification of novel PKR inhibitory chemotypes via integrated molecular modelling and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Interferon-inducible RNA-dependent protein kinase (PKR) is an emerging therapeutic target involved in cancer, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory disorders; however, the discovery of potent and structurally diverse PKR inhibitors remains limited. In this study, we report an integrated computational-experimental strategy for the identification of novel PKR inhibitory chemotypes. Pharmacophore models were generated from flexible docking of structurally diverse reference inhibitors and validated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. To better capture ligand flexibility and addre
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational-experimental approach to identify novel inhibitors of PKR, a therapeutic target in cancer and inflammatory diseases. By combining pharmacophore modeling, flexible docking, and machine learning, the authors discovered new chemotypes with PKR inhibitory activity, expanding the limited chemical diversity of known PKR inhibitors.

papers.title: Quantum dot (QD)-based silicon as an efficient catalyst for the one-pot synthesis of polynuclear acridines: molecular docking investigation of putative anti-tubercular and anti-HIV drug candidates.
papers.abstract: Silicon quantum dots (Si-QDs), a novel class of nanomaterials, display adjustable optical characteristics due to quantum confinement effects, making them promising photocatalysts and reactive species for organic transformations. In this study, Si-QDs were synthesized via the hydrothermal method and analyzed using IR, XRD, TEM, EDX, and SEM techniques. The synthesized Si-QDs were employed to produce 1,8-dioxodecahydroacridine frameworks in a one-pot reaction under solvent-free conditions. Molecular docking studies revealed that multiple acridine derivatives displayed robust multitarget binding
papers.summary: This study reports the synthesis of silicon quantum dots (Si-QDs) via a hydrothermal method and their use as an efficient catalyst for the one-pot, solvent-free synthesis of polynuclear acridines. Molecular docking studies suggest that several of the synthesized acridine derivatives have potential as multitarget anti-tubercular and anti-HIV drug candidates.

papers.title: Rational design, synthesis, and antimicrobial evaluation of novel 1,2,3-triazole hybrids: structure-activity relationships, molecular docking, and DFT studies.
papers.abstract: A series of novel 2,4-dichlorophenyl-1,2,3-triazole derivatives and their structural hybrids incorporating chalcone, hydrazone, thio/semicarbazide, carbamate, and pyrazole moieties were rationally designed, synthesized, and characterized. The antimicrobial activity of the synthesized compounds was evaluated against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, as well as Candida albicans, revealing clear structure-dependent activity profiles. Among the tested compounds, the parent triazole-acetyl scaffold (compound 3) exhibited the most consistent broad-spectrum activity, with MIC values of 22.5 m
papers.summary: This study reports the rational design and synthesis of novel 1,2,3-triazole hybrids with various structural moieties, evaluating their antimicrobial activity against bacteria and fungi. The parent triazole-acetyl scaffold showed the most consistent broad-spectrum activity, and structure-activity relationships were supported by molecular docking and DFT studies.

papers.title: Design and synthesis of isoxazolidine core-based selective COX-2 inhibitors: in vitro inhibitor activity and in silico modeling.
papers.abstract: A novel series of tricyclic isoxazolidine-imidazole derivatives (3a-l) bearing diverse substituted phenyl groups were rationally designed, synthesized, and evaluated as selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitors. The target compounds were efficiently obtained via regio- and diastereoselective 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition of C-aryl-3-methylphenyl nitrones with 1-vinylimidazole. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterization was performed using FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and LC-MS spectrometry. In vitro assays demonstrated potent COX-2 inhibition with minimal COX-1 activity, achieving high selectivity
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of novel isoxazolidine-imidazole derivatives as selective COX-2 inhibitors, with in vitro assays showing potent COX-2 inhibition and high selectivity over COX-1. The compounds were synthesized via a stereoselective 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition and characterized by standard spectroscopic methods, supported by in silico modeling.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanism of Fungal Effector PevD1-NRP Interaction and Discovery of a Small-Molecule Disruptor.
papers.abstract: Verticillium wilt, caused by Verticillium dahliae, is a devastating vascular disease that severely affects cotton and other dicotyledonous crops worldwide. The fungal effector protein PevD1 promotes disease progression by interacting with the host asparagine-rich protein (NRP) and disrupting cryptochrome 2 (CRY2)-mediated signaling; however, the molecular basis of this interaction remains poorly understood. Here, we combined computational modeling, molecular interaction analysis, mutagenesis, and structural biology approaches to investigate the PevD1-NRP-CRY2 regulatory mechanism in Arabidopsi
papers.summary: This study elucidates the molecular mechanism by which the fungal effector PevD1 interacts with the host protein NRP to disrupt CRY2-mediated signaling in Arabidopsis, contributing to Verticillium wilt disease. Using computational modeling, mutagenesis, and structural biology, the authors identify key interaction interfaces and discover a small-molecule disruptor that can block this interaction, offering a potential strategy for disease control.

papers.title: The major diagnostic VSG LiTat 1.3 of the human parasite Trypanosoma brucei gambiense is a trimer in solution.
papers.abstract: Human African trypanosomiasis (HAT) remains a significant health burden in sub-Saharan Africa, with serological diagnosis relying heavily on parasite variant surface glycoproteins (VSGs). Experimentally validated structural studies of VSGs from Trypanosoma brucei gambiense (the main HAT causative agent) are currently lacking despite their diagnostic importance. In this study, we present a thorough characterization of LiTat 1.3, a key VSG in the diagnosis of T. b. gambiense infections, through an integrative structural biology approach encompassing AlphaFold-based structure prediction, analytic
papers.summary: This study provides the first experimentally validated structural characterization of LiTat 1.3, a key variant surface glycoprotein used in diagnosing Human African trypanosomiasis, revealing that it forms a trimer in solution. Using an integrative approach combining AlphaFold predictions and biophysical analyses, the findings fill a critical gap in understanding VSG structure for this pathogen and have direct implications for improving diagnostic tools.

papers.title: Systematic mapping of insertion-tolerant regions enables capsid engineering of an infectious RNA phage.
papers.abstract: RNA phages are attractive platforms for the design of programmable bioparticles, but their development has been constrained by limited knowledge of genomic sites that can tolerate sequence insertion. Here, we combined MuA transposase-mediated in vitro insertion mutagenesis with our established reverse genetics systems to systematically identify insertion-tolerant regions (ITRs) in the RNA phages MS2 and PP7. Screening of 4,555 MS2 and 2,228 PP7 random insertion clones identified 29 and 26 non-redundant ITRs, respectively. We further analyzed and compared these ITRs in the context of RNA genome
papers.summary: This study systematically maps insertion-tolerant regions (ITRs) in the genomes of RNA phages MS2 and PP7 using transposon-mediated mutagenesis and reverse genetics, identifying dozens of sites that can accommodate foreign sequences without disrupting phage infectivity. These ITRs provide a roadmap for engineering RNA phages as programmable bioparticles for applications such as drug delivery and vaccine development.

papers.title: Tetracyclic triterpenes from Chios Mastic Gum act as TGR5 and RORγ modulators.
papers.abstract: Chios mastic gum (CMG) is a natural resin from Pistacia lentiscus L. var. Chia (Anacardiaceae). It contains high concentrations of triterpenoids, with 24Z-masticadienonic acid (24Z-MNA) and 24Z-isomasticadienonic acid (24Z-IMNA) being the predominant compounds. CMG has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory activity in vitro; however, the molecular targets remain unknown.
papers.summary: This study identifies tetracyclic triterpenes from Chios Mastic Gum as modulators of TGR5 and RORγ, two key receptors involved in inflammation and metabolism. The findings suggest these natural compounds may mediate the anti-inflammatory effects of mastic gum through specific molecular targets.

papers.title: Modeling Dual-Range Atomic Interactions with Physicochemical Principles for Molecular Force Fields.
papers.abstract: Machine Learning Force Fields (MLFFs) have emerged as promising tools for accelerating molecular dynamics simulations. However, existing approaches often struggle to capture the geometric characteristics of long-range interactions, including distance and direction, remain sensitive to conformational variations, and lack adaptive mechanisms for balancing short- and long-range forces. To address these limitations, we propose GeoNet , a physicochemical-principle-guided framework for modeling dual-range atomic interactions. GeoNet employs geometric attention over atom-fragment bipartite graphs to
papers.summary: This paper introduces GeoNet, a machine learning force field framework that models both short- and long-range atomic interactions using physicochemical principles and geometric attention over atom-fragment bipartite graphs. It addresses limitations of existing MLFFs in capturing long-range geometric characteristics and balancing force contributions, potentially improving molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Integrated design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and computational mechanistic insights of novel benzanilide derivatives as VEGFR-2 targeted anticancer agents.
papers.abstract: VEGFR-2 is a key regulator of tumor angiogenesis and a validated target in anticancer drug discovery. In this study, a series of novel benzanilide derivatives (7a-7f and 9a-9b) were designed, synthesized, and evaluated as potential VEGFR-2 inhibitors. The design strategy was guided by key pharmacophoric requirements for VEGFR-2 inhibition. All compounds were synthesized successfully and characterized, then screened for in vitro cytotoxic activity against MCF-7, MDA-MB-231, HePG-2, and HCT-116 cancer cell lines, with WI-38 and WISH normal cells used for selectivity assessment. Among the tested
papers.summary: This study reports the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel benzanilide derivatives as VEGFR-2 inhibitors for anticancer therapy. The compounds showed cytotoxic activity against several cancer cell lines with selectivity over normal cells, and computational studies provided mechanistic insights into their binding. This work contributes to the development of new VEGFR-2-targeted anticancer agents.

papers.title: Coumarin-based dual kinase inhibitors targeting CDK6 and VEGFR-2: experimental and computational validation.
papers.abstract: A rational pharmacophore-guided strategy was employed to design and synthesize a series of novel coumarin derivatives as potential dual cyclin-dependent kinase 6 (CDK6) and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) inhibitors. Following structural characterization, the synthesized compounds were evaluated for their anticancer activity against MCF-7, MDA-MB-231, HepG-2, and HCT-116 cancer cell lines, together with normal WI-38 and WISH cells. Among the tested derivatives, compound 7e exhibited the highest potency, with IC50 values ranging from 3.80 to 6.35 µM, while demonstrating
papers.summary: This study describes the design and synthesis of novel coumarin-based dual inhibitors targeting CDK6 and VEGFR-2, with compound 7e showing potent anticancer activity across multiple cancer cell lines. The work combines experimental evaluation with computational validation, offering a promising lead for dual-target cancer therapy.

papers.title: Determinants of substrate specificity in mint pulegone reductase, a double bond reductase of the medium-chain dehydrogenase/reductase superfamily.
papers.abstract: Pulegone reductase from peppermint (Mentha × piperita; MpPulR) is an NADPH-dependent medium-chain dehydrogenase/reductase that catalyzes asymmetric reduction of the C4-C7 double bond of (+)-pulegone to (-)-menthone and (+)-isomenthone. To define the structural determinants of substrate recognition and catalytic turnover, we integrated structure-based modeling (docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations) with experimental mutagenesis and comprehensive substrate profiling. Residues positioned closely to (+)-pulegone in homology-based structural models were subjected to L-Ala-scanning mutage
papers.summary: This study identifies the structural determinants of substrate specificity in mint pulegone reductase, an enzyme involved in menthol biosynthesis, using a combination of molecular modeling, mutagenesis, and substrate profiling. The findings reveal key residues that govern substrate recognition and catalytic turnover, providing insights into the enzyme's mechanism and potential for engineering.

papers.title: Novel tetrazole annulation on benzopyridodiazepine derivatives as inhibitor of tropomyosin kinase B (TrkB): rational design, synthesis, biological evaluation, SAR, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Tropomyosin kinase B (TrkB) is an attractive target for cancer treatment and is emerging as a target for the treatment of neurological disorders, specifically epilepsy, due to its role in regulating neuronal degeneration and inflammation. However, current medications frequently suffer from toxicity, resistance, and poor metabolism. In the present study, four new series of tetrazole annulated benzopyridodiazepine derivatives (26 examples) were synthesized in two steps: intramolecular cyclization with various sets of amines to produce benzopyridodiazepinone derivatives, and then, in the second s
papers.summary: This study describes the design and synthesis of 26 novel tetrazole-annulated benzopyridodiazepine derivatives as inhibitors of tropomyosin kinase B (TrkB), a target for cancer and neurological disorders. The compounds were evaluated for biological activity, structure-activity relationships, and in silico properties, aiming to overcome issues like toxicity and resistance in current treatments.

papers.title: Stabilization of prefusion hMPV F improves manufacturability and protective immunity across hMPV lineages.
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a major cause of pediatric acute lower respiratory tract infections (ALRTIs), yet vaccine development has been hindered by the intrinsic metastability of the prefusion F glycoprotein (pre-F). Here, we used a structure-based design strategy to stabilize hMPV pre-F while preserving neutralization-sensitive epitopes. By applying combined stabilizing elements, including disulfide bonds, a designed salt bridge, and a trimer-interface sequence swap, we generated VM-874, a pre-F-stabilized trimer that was expressed at high levels in 293F cells and exhibited improved th
papers.summary: This study describes a structure-based design approach to stabilize the prefusion F glycoprotein of human metapneumovirus (hMPV), generating a variant called VM-874 that is expressed at high levels and retains neutralization-sensitive epitopes. The stabilized pre-F trimer shows improved manufacturability and elicits protective immunity across hMPV lineages, addressing a key barrier in hMPV vaccine development.

papers.title: A Covalent Organic Framework With Staggered Topology for Mimetic Transmembrane Transport of Hydrated Ions.
papers.abstract: In biological systems, hydrated-ions cross protein channels with exceptional high efficiency through a structural dehydration-compensation mechanism, where protein conformational adjustments contract the channel and enable electron-rich sites to coordinate with ions, offsetting their dehydration energy without external energy input. In this work, we discovered that a typical β-ketoenamine-linked covalent organic framework (COF) with staggered-stacking architectures exhibits a similar mechanism. Although COFs lack dynamic conformational adjustments, the AB-staggered topology generates convergen
papers.summary: This study discovers that a β-ketoenamine-linked covalent organic framework (COF) with staggered-stacking architecture mimics the biological dehydration-compensation mechanism for efficient hydrated-ion transport. The AB-staggered topology creates convergent electron-rich sites that coordinate with ions, offsetting dehydration energy without external input, similar to protein channels. This finding provides a new design principle for synthetic ion-transport materials.

papers.title: Discovery of indazole-carboxamide based USP8 inhibitor for immune activation and antitumor response in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (CRC), which accounts for most CRC cases, responds poorly to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Increasing evidence suggests that the deubiquitinase USP8 maintains PD-L1 protein expression by erasing its K48-linked ubiquitination, thereby preserving membrane PD-L1 and facilitating immune escape. How pharmacological inhibition of USP8 regulates PD-L1 stability and antitumor immunity in CRC, however, has not been fully clarified.
papers.summary: This study reports the discovery of an indazole-carboxamide-based inhibitor of the deubiquitinase USP8, which stabilizes PD-L1 by removing its degradation signal. In colorectal cancer models, USP8 inhibition reduced PD-L1 levels and enhanced antitumor immune responses, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer, which typically does not respond to immune checkpoint inhibitors.

papers.title: Discovery of Novel AURKA Inhibitors for Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) Therapy via a Hybrid Virtual Screening Pipeline, Biological Evaluation and Molecular Dynamics Simulation.
papers.abstract: Aurora kinase A (AURKA) is a pivotal driver of malignant progression and poor prognosis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). In this study, we developed a cascaded AI-driven virtual screening pipeline, integrating sequence-based affinity prediction (PSICHIC), equivariant deep learning docking (KarmaDock), and geometric rescoring (DeepDock) to identify novel AURKA inhibitor candidates. From an in-house 160,000-compound screening library assembled from commercially available collections, three leads (compounds 3, 5, and 8) were selected and subsequently validated via HTRF biochemical assays,
papers.summary: This study presents a hybrid AI-driven virtual screening pipeline that combines sequence-based affinity prediction, deep learning docking, and geometric rescoring to identify novel AURKA inhibitors for triple-negative breast cancer. Three lead compounds were validated biochemically, demonstrating the pipeline's effectiveness in discovering potential therapeutic candidates.

papers.title: SPAN 60 and TWEEN 60 surfactant-based niosomal vesicles: from preparation to molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The role of vesicular systems in the field of drug delivery has led to increased research in the optimization of these novel delivery methods. Niosomes are bilayer structures that are capable of encapsulating lipophilic and hydrophilic compounds. In this study, niosomal systems formed from either Span 60 or Tween 60 non-ionic surfactants were investigated through experimental work and molecular dynamics simulations. Niosomes were prepared using thin-film hydration (TFH) and organic phase injection (OPI) methods and characterized in terms of particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential,
papers.summary: This study investigates niosomal vesicles made from Span 60 or Tween 60 surfactants, combining experimental preparation methods (thin-film hydration and organic phase injection) with molecular dynamics simulations to characterize their properties. The work provides insights into how surfactant type and preparation method affect niosome characteristics, which is relevant for optimizing drug delivery systems.

papers.title: [Preliminary investigation into the mechanisms of thalidomide in inhibiting the malignant transformation of oral leukoplakia].
papers.abstract: This study aims to integrate network pharmacology, machine learning, and survival analysis to preliminarily explore the molecular mechanisms underlying the inhibitory effects of thalidomide on the malignant transformation of oral leukoplakia (OLK).
papers.journal: Hua xi kou qiang yi xue za zhi = Huaxi kouqiang yixue zazhi = West China journal of stomatology
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology, machine learning, and survival analysis to investigate how thalidomide may inhibit the malignant transformation of oral leukoplakia, a precancerous oral condition. The findings provide preliminary molecular insights into thalidomide's potential protective mechanisms.

papers.title: Efficient One-Pot Synthesis of Dibenzoxanthenes Using a Vinylimidazolium-Based Brønsted Acidic Ionic Liquid [VSBIM][Cl]: In Silico Evaluation of Drug-Likeness, ADMET Properties, PASS Analysis, Antiviral Activity Prediction, and Molecular Docking Studies.
papers.abstract: Dibenzoxanthene derivatives have produced considerable interest due to their pharmacological, photophysical, and organic optoelectronic properties. Herein, a facile one-pot methodology was developed for the synthesis of 14-(aryl)-14H-dibenzo[a,j]xanthene derivatives employing 5 mol% of the Brønsted acidic ionic liquid 1-vinyl-3-(4-sulfobutyl) imidazolium chloride [VSBIM][Cl] as an efficient and recyclable catalyst under solvent-free conditions. This protocol enables the condensation of β-naphthol with varied aryl or heteroaryl aldehydes to afford dibenzoxanthenes under neat conditions at 110°C
papers.summary: This paper presents a new, efficient one-pot method for synthesizing dibenzoxanthene derivatives using a recyclable Brønsted acidic ionic liquid catalyst under solvent-free conditions. The authors also performed computational analyses (drug-likeness, ADMET, PASS, antiviral activity prediction, and molecular docking) to explore the potential pharmacological applications of the synthesized compounds.

papers.title: Vorinostat Mitigates Early Brain Injury Following Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Through Modulation of the C3aR1/TGF-β/Smad Pathway.
papers.abstract: Excessive microglial activation after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) contributes to early brain injury (EBI) and poor clinical outcomes. This study explores the role of complement C3a receptor 1 (C3aR1) in microglial activation after SAH and evaluates Vorinostat as a potential therapeutic agent.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of complement C3a receptor 1 (C3aR1) in microglial activation after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and evaluates the therapeutic potential of Vorinostat. The findings suggest that Vorinostat mitigates early brain injury by modulating the C3aR1/TGF-β/Smad pathway, offering a potential treatment strategy for SAH.

papers.title: Elucidating the Antiglycation Potential of Plumbagin Against Methylglyoxal-Induced Glycation of Bovine Liver Catalase.
papers.abstract: Non-enzymatic glycosylation of proteins leads to the formation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs), implicated in oxidative stress and the progression of several chronic diseases. Among the reactive carbonyl compounds, methylglyoxal (MGO) is highly potent in inducing glycoxidative damage by modifying proteins. Herein, we investigated the protective effect of plumbagin, a naphthoquinone derived from Plumbago zeylanica, to counteract MGO-induced glycation of catalase, employing integrated biophysical and computational approaches. AGE-specific fluorescence at 335 and 370 nm, ThT dye fluores
papers.summary: This study investigates whether plumbagin, a plant-derived compound, can protect the enzyme catalase from damage caused by methylglyoxal-induced glycation, a process linked to chronic diseases. Using biophysical and computational methods, the authors find that plumbagin reduces the formation of advanced glycation end products and preserves catalase structure and function, suggesting its potential as an antiglycation agent.

papers.title: Geometric Deep Learning-Based Drug Design Models for Small-Molecule Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Deep neural network (DNN)-based in silico models show great promise in predicting the properties and bioactivities of novel compounds, including small molecules. Among traditional approaches, structure-based drug design (SBDD) remains a fundamental approach for drug discovery using molecular docking, scoring functions, and molecular dynamics simulations. However, these approaches are often constrained by limited flexibility, resolution, and generalizability. Geometric deep learning (GDL) offers a transformative alternative by enabling models to learn directly from non-Euclidean molecular repre
papers.summary: This review discusses how geometric deep learning (GDL) is transforming small-molecule drug design by enabling models to learn directly from non-Euclidean molecular representations, overcoming limitations of traditional structure-based approaches like docking and molecular dynamics. It highlights GDL's potential to improve property prediction and bioactivity assessment for novel compounds.

papers.title: Synthesis of Some Oxime Derivatives as Novel Elastase Inhibitors: Molecular Dynamics Studies and Computational Insight.
papers.abstract: Oximes and oxime ethers are important compounds in organic chemistry, both structurally and in terms of applications. The biological properties of oximes are directly related to the chemical properties of their functional groups, metal-binding capacities, and ability to interact with biological targets in a multifaceted way. This study presents the synthesis of 5-hydroxyimino 2a-b and 5-methoxyimino 2c derivatives from 5-oxo pentanoic acid methyl esters (1a-c) containing phenyl, p-chlorophenyl, and thiophenyl groups, elucidation of their structures through various spectroscopic analysis method
papers.summary: This study synthesizes novel oxime and oxime ether derivatives from 5-oxo pentanoic acid methyl esters and evaluates their potential as elastase inhibitors using molecular dynamics and computational methods. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically, and computational insights suggest they may serve as promising leads for elastase inhibition.

papers.title: Machine learning-guided screening and validation of antioxidant small molecules from Clausena lansium.
papers.abstract: To discover natural antioxidants from Clausena lansium (Lour.) Skeels for food applications, we established a 474-compound database and applied a multiscale workflow integrating ensemble machine learning, molecular docking, structural clustering, molecular dynamics simulations, and quantum chemical calculations. The ensemble models achieved ROC-AUC values of 0.85-0.99 across eight antioxidant assays. Multi-criteria screening yielded 47 candidates, and 30 structurally diverse candidates underwent molecular dynamics simulations. Quercetin 3-arabinoside was prioritized, exhibiting stable non-cova
papers.summary: This study developed a machine learning-guided workflow to screen for natural antioxidants from Clausena lansium, integrating ensemble models, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations. They identified quercetin 3-arabinoside as a promising candidate with stable binding, validated through multi-criteria screening.

papers.title: Identification and characterization of umami peptides from enzymatic hydrolysates of cod skin based on sensory evaluation and molecular simulations.
papers.abstract: Cod skin possesses a pronounced savoury flavour yet remains underutilised as a processing by product. As a potential source of umami peptides, cod skin holds significant development potential. This study employed gel permeation chromatography (GPC), ultrafiltration (UF), sensory evaluation, high-performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and virtual screening to isolate, purify, screen, and identify potential umami peptides from cod skin enzymatic hydrolysate (EHCS). Five potential umami peptides: GDRGFPGER, SSGDQGPAG, SSGPFGE, LPGADDDKF, and GLPGADDKF were screened
papers.summary: This study identified five novel umami peptides from cod skin enzymatic hydrolysates using a combination of sensory evaluation, chromatography, mass spectrometry, and virtual screening. The findings highlight the potential of cod skin, a common processing byproduct, as a valuable source of flavor-enhancing peptides for food applications.

papers.title: Edge-aware GAT-based protein binding sites prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of protein binding sites is crucial for understanding biomolecular interaction mechanisms and for the rational design of drug targets. Traditional predictive methods often struggle to balance prediction accuracy with computational efficiency when capturing complex spatial conformations. To address this challenge, we propose an Edge-aware Graph Attention Network (Edge-aware GAT) model for the fine-grained prediction of binding sites across various biomolecules, including proteins, DNA/RNA, ions, ligands, and lipids. Our method constructs atom-level graphs and integrates
papers.summary: This paper presents an Edge-aware Graph Attention Network (Edge-aware GAT) for predicting protein binding sites across diverse biomolecules, including proteins, DNA/RNA, ions, ligands, and lipids. By integrating edge-aware attention into atom-level graphs, the model improves prediction accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency, offering a robust tool for drug target identification.

papers.title: Effects of different marine surimi addition on the gelling properties of freshwater surimi gels: Protein crosslinking and endogenous enzyme interactions.
papers.abstract: Blending freshwater and marine surimi has been widely applied to improve gel product quality, while the species-dependent effects on gelation remain unclear. This study evaluated the effects of Alaska pollock surimi and hairtail surimi on the gelation properties of silver carp surimi at different blending ratios (0-40%). Alaska pollock surimi enhanced gelation, increasing gel strength, hardness and whiteness. In contrast, hairtail surimi weakened gelation, reducing gel strength and whiteness. Water-state and structural analyses showed that hairtail surimi increased water mobility and generated
papers.summary: This study shows that blending silver carp surimi with Alaska pollock surimi improves gel strength, hardness, and whiteness, while blending with hairtail surimi weakens these properties. The differences are attributed to species-specific protein crosslinking and endogenous enzyme activities, which affect water mobility and gel structure. These findings provide guidance for optimizing mixed-surimi formulations in the food industry.

papers.title: Computational investigation for exploring botanical ingredients as potential negative allosteric modulators targeting metabotropic glutamate receptor 5.
papers.abstract: Metabotropic glutamate receptors are class C G-protein-coupled receptors that respond to the neurotransmitter glutamate. In particular, metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5) has been a valuable drug target for the management of psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders such as fragile X syndrome, autism, depression, anxiety, addiction, and movement disorders through negative allosteric modulators (NAMs). Despite the discovery of several NAMs, limited clinical efficacy was observed, thus preventing them from reaching the clinical stage. Natural products are indispensable, with a plethora
papers.summary: This computational study screens botanical ingredients as potential negative allosteric modulators (NAMs) of metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5), a drug target for psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. The findings identify promising natural compounds that may serve as leads for developing more effective NAMs with better clinical efficacy.

papers.title: Rational Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of New Substituted Dihydropyrimidinones as Antibacterial Agents and β-Lactamase Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: A series of new substituted 1,6-dihydropyrimidinones was designed, synthesized, and biologically evaluated as potential antibacterial candidates and β-lactamase enzyme inhibitors. All the synthesized compounds were tested for their antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, Bacillus subtilis as a gram-positive species whereas Pseudomonas aeruginosa as a gram-negative species was utilized. Most of the compounds exhibited moderate antibacterial activity compared to the reference drug amoxicillin. Furthermore, clinical antibacterial tests were conducted on β-lactamase resistant strains
papers.summary: This study reports the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of new substituted dihydropyrimidinones as antibacterial agents and β-lactamase inhibitors. Most compounds showed moderate antibacterial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria compared to amoxicillin, and were also tested against β-lactamase-resistant strains.

papers.title: Manufacturing and electrostatic surface optimization of CAR-T cells improve therapeutic efficacy in liver malignancies.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has achieved remarkable success in hematologic malignancies, yet demonstrates limited efficacy in solid tumors, including hepatic cancers. T-cell exhaustion and insufficient persistence represent major obstacles. We hypothesized that optimizing both manufacturing processes and CAR structural design could reduce exhaustion and enhance therapeutic outcomes in immunocompetent mouse models of primary and metastatic liver malignancies.
papers.summary: This study shows that optimizing CAR-T cell manufacturing and the electrostatic surface of the CAR construct reduces T-cell exhaustion and improves persistence, leading to better therapeutic efficacy in immunocompetent mouse models of primary and metastatic liver cancer. The findings suggest that combined manufacturing and structural design improvements can overcome key barriers to CAR-T therapy in solid tumors.

papers.title: From structural insight to molecule: Integrative molecular simulations identify candidate pyruvate kinase activators.
papers.abstract: Pyruvate kinase (PKLR) is a key glycolytic enzyme that regulates red blood cell energy homeostasis. Although Mitapivat is the first approved allosteric activator for pyruvate kinase deficiency (PKD), its clinical utility is limited by metabolic and pharmacokinetic challenges, underscoring the need for improved analogues. This study aimed to identify novel Mitapivat-derived scaffolds with enhanced PKLR binding, stability, and drug-like properties using an integrated computational approach. A total of 190 structurally related derivatives were screened through molecular docking, pharmacophore mod
papers.summary: This study used an integrated computational approach, including molecular docking and pharmacophore modeling, to screen 190 Mitapivat-derived compounds as potential pyruvate kinase (PKLR) activators. The goal was to identify novel scaffolds with improved binding, stability, and drug-like properties compared to the approved drug Mitapivat, addressing its metabolic and pharmacokinetic limitations.

papers.title: Prunetin ameliorates myocardial pyroptosis after myocardial infarction by inhibiting the TNF-α/p38 MAPK/ERK pathway.
papers.abstract: The inflammatory response in cardiac tissue after myocardial infarction (MI) plays a critical role in myocardial injury. Prunetin (PRU), a natural flavonoid compound, has notable anti-inflammatory properties; however, its role in post-MI myocardial injury and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates the effects of prunetin, a natural flavonoid with anti-inflammatory properties, on myocardial injury following myocardial infarction (MI). The findings suggest that prunetin ameliorates myocardial pyroptosis (a form of inflammatory cell death) by inhibiting the TNF-α/p38 MAPK/ERK signaling pathway, thereby reducing cardiac inflammation and injury post-MI.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into daidzin from Glycine max against breast cancer via network pharmacology and multi-level molecular modeling.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in women, with around 2.3 million new cases and 670,000 deaths worldwide in 2022. Daidzin, a soy isoflavone glycoside from Glycine max, is a candidate bioactive scaffold, but its breast cancer-relevant mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study used an integrated in silico strategy combining network pharmacology and molecular modeling to prioritize daidzin targets and validate key interactions, with sirtinol as a reference compound. Target prediction identified 101 putative daidzin targets, and intersection with breast cancer-ass
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular modeling to investigate how daidzin, a soy isoflavone, may act against breast cancer. The authors identified 101 putative daidzin targets and validated key interactions, providing mechanistic insights into its potential anti-cancer activity.

papers.title: A report on the mechanisms of sweeteners in four musculoskeletal disorders: Insights from network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Sweeteners are widely-studied food additives linked to metabolism and obesity, yet their musculoskeletal effects remain largely unknown.To investigate the potential effects of sweeteners on the musculoskeletal system, this study integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to systematically analyze the molecular associations between sweetener exposure and intervertebral disc degeneration, myositis, osteoarthritis, and osteoporosis. The results showed that sweeteners may affect musculoskeletal health by interfering with 35 core targets, which are primaril
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to explore how sweeteners might affect musculoskeletal health, identifying 35 core targets linked to intervertebral disc degeneration, myositis, osteoarthritis, and osteoporosis. The findings suggest sweeteners could interfere with these targets, potentially impacting musculoskeletal disorders, though experimental validation is needed.

papers.title: Rational Design and Optimization of MCh-AMP1: A Stable α-Helical Antifungal Peptide with Enhanced Activity Against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Candida infections, particularly those caused by Candida albicans, are a growing threat to global health, exacerbated by increasing antifungal resistance. Traditional antifungal treatments are becoming increasingly ineffective due to resistance mechanisms, highlighting the need for innovative therapeutic solutions.
papers.summary: This study describes the rational design and optimization of MCh-AMP1, a stable α-helical antifungal peptide with enhanced activity against Candida albicans. The work addresses the growing problem of antifungal resistance by developing a novel peptide-based therapeutic candidate.

papers.title: Computational design of immunogenic peptide-ligand conjugates for targeted therapy against Nipah virus infection.
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) poses a major risk to global public health due to its high infectivity and associated mortality rates. Currently, no licensed vaccines or antiviral medications are available for NiV infection, leaving clinical management limited to supportive care. The viral receptor glycoprotein responsible for binding NiV to host cell receptors (ephrin-B2/B3) represents an ideal therapeutic target. This study proposes a novel peptide-ligand conjugate (PLC) immunotherapeutic approach that exploits pre-existing immune responses in NiV-endemic populations to selectively target and eliminate in
papers.summary: This study computationally designs peptide-ligand conjugates (PLCs) that target the Nipah virus receptor-binding glycoprotein, aiming to exploit pre-existing immune responses for a novel immunotherapeutic approach. The work addresses the urgent need for treatments against Nipah virus, for which no licensed vaccines or antivirals currently exist.

papers.title: A Comprehensive In-Silico Pipeline for the Discovery of Non-toxic, Stable Antimicrobial Peptides From Databases for Targeting Multi-Drug Resistant K. pneumoniae.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae has significantly reduced the effectiveness of conventional antibiotics, highlighting the need for alternative therapeutic strategies. This study employed a comprehensive in silico pipeline to identify antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) targeting the essential DNA replication initiator protein DnaA. A total of 28,361 peptide sequences were collected from publicly available AMP databases and sequentially filtered based on peptide length, net charge, GRAVY score, instability index, antimicrobial activity, toxicity, hemolytic potential,
papers.summary: This study developed a computational pipeline to screen 28,361 peptide sequences from public databases for antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) that target the essential protein DnaA in multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. The pipeline filters peptides based on physicochemical properties, toxicity, and hemolytic potential, ultimately identifying promising non-toxic, stable AMP candidates for further experimental validation.

papers.title: In silico high-throughput screening system for INMT activators in prostate cancer therapy.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality in men, with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) posing significant therapeutic challenges due to drug resistance mediated by the androgen receptor (AR) signaling pathway. Indolethylamine-N-methyltransferase (INMT), a tumor-suppressive enzyme downregulated in CRPC, regulates pathways associated with apoptosis and proliferation. Leveraging a structure-based drug design strategy, this study aimed to identify novel INMT agonists for CRPC therapy. Virtual screening of the ChemDiv compound library (guided by the
papers.summary: This study used a structure-based virtual screening approach to identify potential activators of the tumor-suppressive enzyme INMT, which is downregulated in castration-resistant prostate cancer. By screening the ChemDiv compound library, the authors identified promising drug candidates that could restore INMT activity and counteract androgen receptor-mediated drug resistance.

papers.title: Multifunctional nanozyme platforms in central nervous system therapies: from rational design to translational medicine.
papers.abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) disorders-including ischemic stroke, traumatic brain/spinal cord injury, Parkinson's disease, and Alzheimer's disease-have long faced limitations in achieving functional recovery and disease-modifying therapies because of their complex pathophysiological mechanisms. Traditional therapies are often constrained by poor penetration across CNS barriers, limited participation in multiple pathological cascades, and insufficient persistence of therapeutic effects. Nanozymes are a class of nanomaterials with enzyme-like catalytic activity and tunable physicochemical proper
papers.summary: This review discusses the design and application of multifunctional nanozymes for treating central nervous system disorders, highlighting their ability to cross CNS barriers and target multiple pathological pathways. It covers rational design strategies and translational challenges, positioning nanozymes as a promising therapeutic platform for conditions like stroke and Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Rhizosphere microecological characteristics associated with tobacco root-knot nematode disease.
papers.abstract: Root-knot nematode disease poses a serious threat to the production of tobacco and other crops, but the rhizosphere microecological response mechanisms during disease development remain unclear. In this study, we collected rhizosphere soil from healthy and diseased tobacco plants in typical tobacco-growing areas of Kunming, Yunnan Province, China, and we systematically identified the differences in soil physicochemical properties, enzyme activities, and the microbial community composition and structure based on 16S rDNA and ITS amplicon sequencing. Compared to healthy rhizosphere soil, disease
papers.summary: This study characterizes the rhizosphere microecology of tobacco plants affected by root-knot nematode disease, comparing soil physicochemical properties, enzyme activities, and microbial communities between healthy and diseased plants. The findings reveal distinct shifts in bacterial and fungal community composition associated with disease, providing insights into the soil microecological response mechanisms underlying nematode infestation.

papers.title: Bacteriophage lysins: a promising strategy for combating foodborne pathogens in food safety.
papers.abstract: Food safety is a major public concern, with foodborne pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus, Listeria monocytogenes, Clostridium perfringens, and Vibrio parahaemolyticus causing millions of infections and significant economic losses annually. Phage and endolysin therapies have emerged as promising environmentally friendly strategies for pathogen control. Bacteriophage lytic enzymes, which are proteins produced during the late stage of phage infection, offer advantages over whole phages, including rapid bactericidal action, a broad antibacterial spectrum, and a low risk of inducing resistance
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of bacteriophage lysins (endolysins) as a novel strategy to combat foodborne pathogens, highlighting their advantages over whole phages, such as rapid action, broad spectrum, and low resistance risk. It emphasizes their potential as environmentally friendly alternatives for food safety applications.

papers.title: Licensed and investigational TLR4 agonists as vaccine adjuvants: structural basis, clinical progress, and future directions.
papers.abstract: The development of innovative vaccine platforms, including protein subunit and nucleic acid vaccines, has advanced rapidly and established new technical paradigms for infectious disease prophylaxis. Nonetheless, many next-generation vaccines display suboptimal intrinsic immunogenicity owing to restricted antigenic complexity, resulting in inadequate protective immunity when delivered without adjuvants. Aluminum-containing adjuvants, the most widely deployed clinical adjuvants, primarily potentiate humoral immunity but elicit modest cellular immune responses, thereby failing to satisfy the immu
papers.summary: This review examines licensed and investigational TLR4 agonists as vaccine adjuvants, focusing on their structural basis, clinical progress, and future directions. It highlights the limitations of current aluminum-based adjuvants in inducing cellular immunity and discusses how TLR4 agonists can enhance both humoral and cellular responses for next-generation vaccines.
